The model selects one action type per decision. Optional payloads not used by that type remain null.
Path
What it executes
What this does not imply
execute
1–6 generic segments; measured completion; up to 240 control steps per sequence.
No object recognition, grasp certificate or collision-free path guarantee.
motion
A numerical pose/gripper target for 1–5 control steps.
Target may not be reached within that short grant.
macro
Optional legacy hold, turn, place_on or release, with its own prerequisites.
A semantic plan intent is not proof that a native macro implements it.
observe / finish
Fresh observation, or a completion claim followed by observation.
Neither action sets official success.
v7’s measured acceleration in these tests came from execute fragments; native macro actions were zero.
t6_009, decision 3: the model supplies the sequence; the same generic executor handles both stages.

Explicit stages
Close until local measured conditions pass, then lift from the actual segment-entry pose.

Visual confirmation belongs to the model
After the lift, inspect whether the mug moved with the gripper. Stable gap alone is insufficient.
Shown: execution payload excerpt.
The controller converts pose error into bounded OSC commands at 20 Hz.

Task-independent code does not establish that all tasks or spatial meanings are supported correctly.
Reusable implementation

Five fragments: move_to_pose, move_relative, approach, set_gripper, wait.

Measured state and explicit handoffs.
No task IDs, object names or predefined task coordinates in the fragment executor.

Model-selected route, grasp and checkpoints.
Limits of the current interface

Input: RGB, robot pose/gap/joints, camera and tool geometry, action feedback.

No hidden object poses, depth, contact identities or goal predicates.

Fragment constraints rely on model interpretation; there is no whole-arm collision planner.
Local feedback is proprioceptive. Fresh visual reasoning happens at model decision boundaries.
All tests use existing LIBERO scenes; no synthetic trajectory or replay is substituted for a task result.

Outcome / timing
Raw LIBERO goal; separate strict physical audit; contacts recorded. Control time excludes video and preparation.
The agent changes its numerical route and hand configuration while fragments execute the repeated control.

Step 1543 · Before user stop.
Pudding released; target relation still false.
Stopped by the user at 1,544 steps and 28 model decisions; net elapsed control time 12:35.
Mug transfer
Approach, close, test-lift, carry, lower, release and withdraw in six decisions.
Pudding descent blocked
Fingers contact the tabletop. The fragment yields on stall; the model initially suspects a joint limit.
Grasp recovered
After another blocked descent, close at the reached height and test-lift. The pudding follows.
Placement revised
Regrasp and reposition; change wrist pitch to improve reach. Final center still misses the goal region.
Framework right_of = world +x is not the same as the benchmark’s named plate-right region.

Official
target region

Semantic issue
Shared instructions tie “right” to +x. Initial placements follow that assumption, and later recovery must work around it.

Terminal result
Pudding COM ≈ (0.1874, 0.1704) m.
x is within the official range.
y is about 20.4 mm beyond its upper edge.
Directions need an explicit, task-grounded reference frame.
The model still selects targets. The fragment controller supplies almost all per-step motor commands.

1,197 fragment actions / 10 direct actions / 0 native macro actions
20 execute grants; 1,207 total control steps.

1,538 fragment actions / 6 direct actions / 0 native macro actions
26 execute grants; 1,544 total control steps.

The useful combination: model-level perception, planning and recovery + reusable measured execution. These percentages measure command attribution, not the fraction of intelligence supplied by either side.
These are conclusions from the recorded tests, not new changes or validated future performance.
Retain

Model ownership of the full task.

Longer measured fragments where targets are clear.

Explicit gripper stages, checkpoints and cause-preserving feedback.

Separate task outcome, physical quality and execution timing.
Next general improvements

Ground directional relations in an explicit frame instead of a universal axis convention.

Verify whole-object placement from new observations.

Improve contact/cause feedback and route quality.

Evaluate multiple tasks and resets before claiming generality.
The English UI is a language-only update. The recorded v7 controller and evaluator were not changed for these slides.
Saved recordings only. No new simulator episode, model request or smoke test was used to build this deck.
